data.name: PTEN
data.description: Phosphatase that erases PIP3 and so shuts down the PI3K arm. One of the most frequently lost tumour suppressors in human cancer, and one of the most common ways this pathway is left switched on without its growth-factor brake.
data.description_beginner: A tumor-suppressing enzyme that erases the 'go' signal generated by PI3K, shutting that branch of the pathway down. It's one of the genes most frequently lost in human cancer, and losing it is one of the most common ways this pathway is left switched on without its growth-factor brake.

studies.title: PTEN regulates microtubule polymerization via mTORC2, but not mTORC1, in peripheral sensory neurons
studies.authors: Evans S; Reglewski J; Rose H; Lewis C; Nayak A; Minsky C; McNeil E; Knowles B; Wang W; Li M; Luikart BW; Hong J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse peripheral sensory neuron cultures (Pten-KO with Raptor or Rictor co-deletion, both sexes)
studies.finding: Uses Raptor (mTORC1) versus Rictor (mTORC2) co-deletion on a Pten-knockout background to ask which complex carries the growth signal to the microtubule cytoskeleton. Suppressing mTORC2 — but not mTORC1 — returns the accelerated microtubule polymerisation and neuronal hypertrophy of Pten-KO neurons to wild-type levels, and the effect is confined to the axonal growth cone rather than the proximal axon shaft. A clean genetic dissection on the comparatively thin mTORC2 side of the pathway.

relations.mechanism: PTEN erases PIP3, undoing PI3K. Losing PTEN is one of the commonest ways a tumour leaves this whole axis switched on without an upstream signal.
relations.mechanism_beginner: PTEN erases the lipid signal that PI3K makes. Losing PTEN is one of the most common ways cancers keep this whole pathway switched on without any signal from outside.
relations.context: The 'inhibits' label describes the net effect on signalling, not the enzyme itself: PTEN does not inhibit PI3K catalytically. It dephosphorylates PIP3, PI3K's lipid product, erasing the signal downstream of the enzyme rather than blocking PI3K's activity.
relations.boundary: The cancer genetics here is mouse work (GUE2009). The biochemical step itself, PTEN dephosphorylating PIP3, has no dedicated paper in this corpus.
relations.note: MAJ2004 was removed from this edge on 2026-09-21: it used Akt-transgenic mice and never manipulated PTEN, so it could not support this step and should not have been setting the edge's tier and species.
